html:
King of the Franks from 768 and the first emperor in the West since the fall of Rome. He built the Carolingian Empire, which covered most of what is now France, Germany, the Low Countries and northern Italy.

He spent most of his reign at war:

  • He conquered the Lombard kingdom of Italy in 774, leaving only the southern Lombard duchies such as Benevento outside his rule.
  • He fought the Saxons for some thirty years and forced them to become Christian.
  • His armies broke the power of the Avars in the 790s and carried off their treasure.
  • He pushed into Spain and set up a border march against the Muslims.

On Christmas Day 800 Pope Leo III crowned him emperor in Rome (Charlemagne crowned emperor). This tied the papacy to the Frankish kings and later fed the idea of the Holy Roman Empire.

From his palace at Aachen he gathered scholars, ordered schools at churches and monasteries, and had old texts copied in a clear new script. Much of what survives of Latin literature comes down through these copies.

His son Louis the Pious kept the empire together, but in 843 his grandsons split it. The parts became West Francia, the seed of France, and East Francia, the seed of Germany.
